text:
maya: Heads up — p95 for streaming RPCs in us-west jumped from ~120ms to ~800ms after 03:00 UTC. Noticed this right after a partner started a large non-streaming bulk embedding run.
aj: ugh, saw that alert. Are streaming requests getting starved by batch jobs on the same GPU pools?
maya: Looks that way. GPU util across the cluster hit ~98% on the long-tail nodes. The scheduler queued many streaming requests behind long synchronous runs.
linh: We always risk that when we don't isolate latency-sensitive work. Any logs showing queue lengths?
sam: stack traces show wait on q:request-queue, also a few timeouts in the async worker. Metrics: streaming-inflight peaked, and batch-jobs kept occupying slots for 30–120s.
maya: Short idea: soft reservation credits for low-latency path. Give streaming requests a small guaranteed share and let batch use leftover. Could be implemented as token-bucket at the executor level.
aj: We tried strict partitioning earlier and it wasted cycles during low batch load. Soft reservations + burst credits sounds promising. How do we backpressure batch jobs gracefully?
linh: We can expose a backpressure signal to the API gateway: when headroom < X, start returning 503-ish advisory to batch clients or queue them in a slower retention queue. Also throttle by tenant weight.
sam: Example policy I sketched:
```yaml
admission:
  low_latency_reservation: 10% # keep 10% of GPU capacity available for streaming
  burst_pool: 25% # extra capacity borrowable for short bursts
  preemptible_window: 2s # how long a batch job can hold a slot before being preempted
  tenant_priority: true
```
maya: Love it. Preemption + short grace should keep SLOs but still let big jobs make progress. We need to decide how to implement preemption safely (checkpointing KV cache?).
aj: For long seq generation preemption is messy. But for embeddings it's safe: it's stateless and resumable. Maybe only preempt non-checkpointed jobs.
linh: Also we should consider admission at the gateway: give streaming a lower cost for admission scoring (cost = estimated_tokens * weight). If estimated cost is high and headroom low, reject or queue the request with a Retry-After header.
sam: We could add an explicit header clients can set: `X-Redwood-Priority: realtime|bulk`. For untrusted clients we apply defaults and rate limits.
maya: We'll need telemetry too: per-tenant qlen, preemptions, retries, and SLO impact. Ops-bot, can you add a dashboard panel?
ops-bot: @maya done — created panel "rt_vs_bulk_admission" showing p50/p95/p99 streaming latency, batch concurrency, headroom. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/rtvbulk
aj: Nice. Next step: rollout admission config as a canary in us-west-a only, keep dedicated low-latency pool disabled until we validate.
maya: Agree. Also add an automated fallback: if preemption rate > 2% for 5m, increase reservation to 20%.
linh: One more thought: network egress contention caused slight stalls — some workers were waiting on checkpoint writes to S3 during preemption which extended hold time. We should make checkpoint writes async w/ local buffering.
sam: Good catch. I'll open a small RFC for async checkpointing and separate the upload worker so it doesn't block GPU slot release.
maya: I'll make the admission config PR and tag you all. Let's keep the canary small and monitor. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: maya started a canary rollout for `admission/rt-bulk-v1` to us-west-a (3 hosts). Canaries: 3/3 healthy so far.
